features.name: Lock timeout settings
features.description: Default lock timeout is 10 seconds in on-premise environments and 35 seconds in SaaS instances. When a session waiting for a lock exceeds this timeout, it is dropped with an error message.
caveats: SQL query timeout in Business Central is around 30 minutes

features.name: Read uncommitted isolation level
features.description: Default isolation level for get or find set functions which executes a select query with read uncommitted table hint. No locks are requested but allows possible dirty reads.
caveats: Allows dirty reads of inconsistent or uncommitted data

features.name: Read committed isolation level
features.description: Isolation level that issues short-lived shared locks on every record being read. Locks are acquired for a fraction of a second only to verify access is allowed before being immediately released.
caveats: Behavior differs between on-premise and cloud: on-premise uses locks by default, cloud with read committed snapshot isolation uses non-locking reads

features.name: Repeatable read isolation level
features.description: Isolation level where shared lock is acquired and held until the end of the transaction until it is committed or rolled back.

features.name: Update lock isolation level
features.description: Lock type applied when calling lock table or read isolation update lock. Used to indicate intent to modify a record.

features.name: Exclusive lock
features.description: Lock type acquired on any record being modified through modify, insert, or delete operations. Ensures no other sessions can access the record while it is being modified or deleted.

features.name: Lock compatibility matrix
features.description: Matrix from SQL Server documentation that defines which lock types can coexist on the same resource. The crossing of rows and columns indicates if simultaneous access can be allowed between two sessions holding or requesting different lock types.
caveats: This is a reduced version; full table available in Microsoft SQL Server documentation

features.name: Intent lock hierarchy
features.description: Lock sequence applies intent locks on table level first, then data page level, and finally record-level locks. Intent locks of any type are always compatible with each other.

features.name: Lock escalation threshold
features.description: When reading approximately 5,000 records with long-living locks, lock escalation occurs, converting row-level locks to a table-level update lock. This is the only way to completely lock a table.
caveats: The 5,000 number is approximate and can be higher

features.name: Lock table statement
features.description: Lock table statement is obsolete and outdated. It has more or less the same effect as applying update lock with read isolation but creates unexpected side effects.
caveats: Obsolete functionality kept for backward compatibility

features.name: Circular deadlock detection
features.description: SQL Server lock monitor checks for circular deadlock situations approximately every 5 seconds. When two or more transactions hold locks on different records and request incompatible locks on each other's resources, deadlock occurs.

features.name: Lock conversion deadlock
features.description: A second type of deadlock on a single record that occurs when two transactions read the same record with repeatable read isolation and both attempt to convert shared locks to exclusive locks.

features.name: Lock hierarchy and lock types
features.description: Demonstration of SQL Server lock hierarchy including intent exclusive locks on table, data pages, and exclusive locks on individual records. Shows how locks escalate through different levels.
caveats: SQL Server behavior specific
demonstrated on on-premise configuration

features.name: Lock timeout with concurrent operations
features.description: When a session holds a table-level exclusive lock due to escalation, other sessions attempting to access the table encounter lock timeouts because they cannot obtain intent locks.
caveats: occurs when operations overlap or interleave
timeout is the error message users see

features.name: Read committed snapshot isolation
features.description: On SaaS instances, read committed snapshot isolation is enabled by default, allowing read operations to work without blocking on table-level exclusive locks held by concurrent write operations.
caveats: only on SaaS by default
on-premise requires manual configuration
has own side effects like right skew

features.name: Repeatable read lock escalation
features.description: Lock escalation can occur with shared locks during repeatable read isolation when reading a large range of records, preventing concurrent modifications outside that range.
caveats: occurs with repeatable read isolation
affects both read and write operations

features.name: Modify in loop pattern
features.description: Alternative to bulk modify all operations where records are modified one at a time in a loop to avoid lock escalation by staying below the 5000 lock threshold per statement.
caveats: performance trade-off for safety
demonstration in this window shows incomplete/failed attempt

features.name: SaaS vs on-premise concurrency behavior differences
features.description: Concurrency behavior differs significantly between SaaS and on-premise deployments due to different default isolation levels and configurations, requiring testing in both environments.
caveats: on-premise defaults differ from SaaS
requires dual testing strategy

features.name: Record-level modify in loops
features.description: Modifying records one-by-one in a loop instead of using modify all avoids escalation but causes significant performance degradation, taking 2.5 to 3 seconds versus 30 to 50 milliseconds for bulk operations.
caveats: Very slow performance
Holds 20,000 individual granular locks

features.name: Chunked update strategy
features.description: Splitting large updates into smaller chunks below the escalation threshold balances performance and concurrency by avoiding full table locks while maintaining reasonable speed.
caveats: Requires careful tuning of chunk size
Needs monitoring of escalation threshold

features.name: If-not-is-empty guard rail pattern
features.description: A common pattern where code checks if a range is empty before calling modify all or delete all, historically applied to prevent locking issues but often used unnecessarily.
caveats: Often applied randomly without proper understanding
May provide false sense of security

features.name: Lock escalation with repeatable read
features.description: When repeatable read isolation level is used, shared locks can escalate to table-level locks, preventing subsequent modify all or delete all operations that require intent exclusive locks.
caveats: Escalation happens when there is risk from different session
Intent exclusive lock incompatible with shared table lock

features.name: Classic update lock deadlock
features.description: A deadlock occurs when two sessions acquire update locks on different records and then attempt to lock each other's records, causing circular wait. The database randomly terminates one session based on rollback cost.
caveats: Session termination is somewhat random
Depends on deadlock priority and rollback cost estimation

features.name: Repeatable read conversion deadlock
features.description: Two sessions both read the same record with repeatable read, then both attempt to modify it. One session succeeds in converting to update lock and then exclusive lock, while the other is terminated due to conflicting lock conversions.
caveats: Lock conversion from shared to update to exclusive
Simultaneous conversion attempts cause deadlock

features.name: SEMAPHORE lock for entry posting
features.description: Classic Dynamics NAV approach where each session posting a new entry locks the last entry, does its posting, inserts the new record, releases the lock, and commits the transaction. This serializes the entire process.
caveats: Creates lock timeouts under high load
Completely serializes the posting process
Clients must wait in a long queue

features.name: Number sequence for entry numbering
features.description: Alternative approach where entry numbers are obtained from a number sequence instead of reading and locking the last entry. The number sequence is non-locking, allowing all sessions to get the next number simultaneously.
caveats: Still requires setting up a number series with number sequence underneath

features.name: Auto increment primary key for entries
features.description: Using auto increment on the primary key field instead of number sequence or manual locking. Allows all sessions to post simultaneously in one second.
caveats: Disables insert buffering completely
Each insert immediately translates to SQL statement instead of being buffered
Can cause performance loss with high-volume entry generation like multi-line sales invoices
Does not provide validation for duplicate entries or business logic checks

features.name: Availability checking with validation
features.description: Adding validation functions to check availability before posting entries, such as verifying seat availability in the cinema ticket booking scenario. Works reliably with serialized SEMAPHORE lock approach because no concurrent actions occur simultaneously.
caveats: Cannot be reliably used with non-locking approaches like number sequences or auto increment without additional race condition handling

features.name: Sequential record insertion with validation
features.description: Approach where records are inserted one by one sequentially with availability checks in between. Provides absolute reliability that no concurrent conflicts occur but results in very slow performance.
caveats: very slow performance
no true parallelism

features.name: Number sequence with validation
features.description: Attempting to add validation checks using number sequence fields. Allows parallel execution but shared locks acquired during reads permit other sessions to see stale data, allowing duplicate entries to be created despite validation logic.
caveats: unreliable - allows duplicates
shared locks permit stale reads
simultaneous reads bypass validation

features.name: Update lock by entity code
features.description: Attempting to acquire update locks on the last entry for a specific entity (cinema code), allowing sessions booking different entities to run in parallel while serializing within each entity. Can cause table scan problems when SQL Server chooses scan-based execution plans.
caveats: table scans cause unintended lock blocking
can serialize different entities unexpectedly
difficult to debug in production
not recommended for production use

features.name: Segmented primary key design
features.description: Redesigning the primary key to include the entity code (cinema code) as the leading column, causing data to be physically clustered by entity on storage. This enables parallel access across entities while avoiding table scan lock problems.
caveats: improved performance over previous approach but still uses entry table

features.name: Dedicated lock table for allocation
features.description: Creating a separate allocation table (cinema allocation) with entity code and seat number as the primary key, moving the symbol for lock away from the heavily-accessed entry table. Sessions lock the allocation record before validating and inserting entries.
caveats: requires additional table design
lock held only during critical section

features.name: IsEmpty checks as symptom vs root cause treatment
features.description: IsEmpty checks on locked tables are perceived as a quick fix but often mask underlying design problems. Using IsEmpty is fast but developers may be treating symptoms rather than addressing the real concurrency issue.
caveats: Performance of IsEmpty is not the issue
Problem is architectural misuse

features.name: Sequential GUID implementation in Business Central
features.description: GUID used as primary key in Business Central is sequential, not random, following a newer algorithm (version 5 or 6) that ensures sequential ordering to reduce SQL page scanning and locking.
caveats: Only applies to GUIDs in Business Central
Version number not precisely recalled by speaker

features.name: Lock threshold estimation at 5000 blocks
features.description: SQL Server lock count threshold is approximately 5000 blocks including table metadata and data pages. Exact lock count cannot be determined precisely, but developers can use approximation.
caveats: Only approximation possible
Includes metadata and table structure locks

features.name: If Not Inserted pattern and buffered insert impact
features.description: Using If Not Inserted to check for duplicate records breaks buffered insert optimization, forcing immediate execution of insert queries instead of batching them, and adds error handling overhead.
caveats: Microsoft code in BC28 has begun removing this pattern in some places
Error handling adds additional latency

features.name: Cache synchronization in scale-out scenarios
features.description: Inserts are always cached, but in scale-out or multi-instance deployments, cache synchronizes approximately every 30 seconds, creating window of data inconsistency.
caveats: Only applies to scale-out or multiple NST instances
Synchronization timing is approximate

features.name: Connection pooling prevents session-lock association
features.description: Business Central connection pooling makes it impossible to directly associate a BC session with a specific SQL connection in AL code, as connections can change between transactions.
caveats: Limitation of AL language
Requires workarounds for diagnostics

features.name: Optimistic locking vs pessimistic locking tradeoff
features.description: Optimistic locking approach assumes resource availability and checks on insert via primary key constraint rather than acquiring locks beforehand, potentially reducing lock contention but increasing failed insert probability.
caveats: Trade-off between lock contention and retry rate
Higher chance of failed inserts with optimistic approach

features.name: Find set with update lock parameter
features.description: The Find Set method with a boolean parameter controls whether update locks are acquired when reading records. True applies FOR UPDATE table hint acquiring update locks, False uses read uncommitted or committed isolation levels depending on Business Central version.
caveats: Behavior differs between Business Central versions 25-26 and earlier versions
